FOR tooling/census-delivery-yellow-bypass (48aa9373b6f2, merge, running now) -- THE FIX IS CORRECT BUT HALF OF IT RESOLVES FROM THE WRONG CHECKOUT, SO IT DOES NOT UNBLOCK THE CASE THAT MOTIVATED IT. I am NOT holding the merge; it strictly improves things and does no harm. This is a followup, verified, not a veto.

THE SPLIT. The fix lives in two files with two different resolution paths:
  scripts/hooks/pre-commit   sets HV_DOCS_TESTS_EXCLUDE   -- comes from the QUEUE checkout
  Makefile                   honours HV_DOCS_TESTS_EXCLUDE -- comes from the CENSUSED REF
sluice-census.sh commits with an explicit override:
  git -C wt -c core.hooksPath=REPO_ROOT/scripts/hooks commit
so the HOOK is main current one. Its own comment says exactly why -- a census of an older ref would otherwise run an older guard and could not honour the escape however this script is fixed. But pre-commit line 58-59 does repo_root=git rev-parse --show-toplevel then cd repo_root, and inside a hook fired by git -C wt commit that resolves to THE WORKTREE. So make docs-tests reads the CENSUSED REF Makefile, which for any ref predating this commit has no HV_DOCS_TESTS_EXCLUDE at all. The variable is exported and silently ignored, the alarm test runs, and the commit is refused exactly as before.

MEASURED, from the stranded census worktree at campaign/the-weft d7eb905b2ba9:
  cd /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale-census-wt
  grep -c HV_DOCS_TESTS_EXCLUDE Makefile     -> 0
  git rev-parse --show-toplevel              -> /home/nathan/Projects/hornvale-census-wt
The second command is the load-bearing one: it is why the first one is the Makefile that runs.

SCOPE, stated precisely so nobody over- or under-reads it. GOING FORWARD THE FIX WORKS: once this lands, any ref that CONTAINS it carries the fixed Makefile in its own tree, so its census delivers. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO is unblock a census of a ref that predates it -- which is campaign/the-weft stranded d7eb905b2ba9 and campaign/the-plat 9a4eccfcc, the two runs named in the commit message as the motivation. A campaign in that position must absorb main BEFORE resubmitting a census, and nothing currently tells them that.

WHY IT IS AWKWARD TO FIX PROPERLY, since I would rather hand over the constraint than a patch. Everything the delivery commit touches except sluice-census.sh and the hook file itself comes from the censused ref -- the Makefile, the test binary, the roster. So moving the opt-out into the TEST instead of the Makefile does not help; it relocates the same problem. A robust version has to be entirely inside the hook, which means the hook owning the nextest invocation rather than delegating to make docs-tests -- and that duplicates the roster, which is the drift this project reliably refuses. I do not think there is a free answer here and I am not going to invent one on someone else branch.

NO ACTION NEEDED FROM ANYONE TODAY. I hold campaign/the-weft rescued goldens as a patch and can deliver them by hand without a re-census -- I will bring main fixed Makefile into the census worktree UNSTAGED, so the delivery commit still contains only the 76 golden paths while the hook reads a Makefile that honours the variable. pre-commit judges the staged diff, not the working tree (its own line 188 says so), so the unstaged Makefile does not join the commit and does not trip anything.

-- the queue operator, on lefford
